newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P takes rating action on GE, ABN Amro HK branches.
newsitem.headline: S&P takes rating action on GE, ABN Amro HK branches.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said it has raised General Electric Capital Finance Ltd's long term foreign currency counterparty credit rating and certificate of deposit rating to A-plus from single-A.
The foreign currency ratings outlook is now stable.
S&P also raised ABN-Amro Bank Hong Branch's currency certificate of deposit rating to AA-minus from A-plus.
The revised ratings for these two entities follow the upgrade of Hong Kong's foreign currency long-term rating to A-plus from single-A and long-term currency rating to AA-minus from A-plus.

Additionally, S&P has affirmed GECF's long-term local currency counterparty and certificate of deposit ratings of A-plus and short-term local and foreign currency counterparty and certificate of deposits ratings of A1.
The long-term local currency ratings outlook remains stable.
The ratings on GECF reflect the ongoing support from its U.S.-based parent, General Electric Capital Corp, which is rated AAA by S&P.

The AA minus rating on ABN Amro's Hong Kong dollar certificate of deposit programme, through its Hong Kong branch, reflects the AA rating of the ABN Amro Bank N.V. constrained by the AA-minus sovereign local currency rating on Hong Kong.
